title: Hosted API Model Rollout Runbook
author: Ava Chen
body:
h1. Purpose
This runbook describes the operational procedure for rolling out a new model version to the Redwood Hosted API in a safe, observable way. It is written for Platform Oncall, Release Engineering, and the Model Onboarding team.

h1. Scope
Applies to: Hosted API traffic served through the public gateway (redwoodapi) and standard routing policies (routerd).
Not covered: Dedicated-only releases, Private deployments, and SDK releases (see Release Engineering playbooks).

h1. Definitions
* Model version: a specific entry in the model registry (e.g., rw/llama-3.1-70b:2025-11-15).
* Rollout: controlled movement of production traffic from the current stable version to the new version.
* Canary: small percentage of production traffic intentionally routed to the new version.
* Fallback: policy-driven automatic reroute to last-known-good version when gates are violated.

h1. Ownership and roles
* Driver (required): Platform Oncall (eng-platform)
* Approver (required): SRE representative (eng-sre)
* Model owner (required): Applied ML or Runtime onboarding owner
* Comms owner (as needed): Oncall Comms (see comms playbook)

h1. Preconditions (must be true before starting)
# Model is registered and marked "ready_for_prod" in the model registry.
# Perf canary job exists and has a green baseline against the current stable version.
# Required dashboards and alerts are present for this model route (see: Hosted API rollout monitoring dashboards and alerts).
# The current stable model version is recorded as "last_known_good" for the route.
# No active major incidents on Hosted API; error budget is not in burn (see SLO gates doc).

h1. Procedure

h2. 1) Create a rollout ticket and announce
# Create a tracking item in Linear (ENG-*) titled "Rollout: <route> -> <new_version>" and link the relevant PR(s).
# Post in #eng-releases with: route, current stable version, new version, planned start time, and driver.
# If the model is customer-visible (default), notify #support and #customer-success with the same summary.

h2. 2) Validate configuration in staging
# Update staging routing policy to mirror intended production policy.
# Send at least 30 minutes of representative traffic replay (or synthetic prompts) to staging.
# Confirm: token accounting is correct, streaming works, function/tool calling behavior unchanged (if applicable), and no new auth failures.

h2. 3) Start production canary
# Set production routing weight to 1% for new version on the route.
# Ensure fallback policy is enabled and points to last-known-good for the route.
# Start the perf-canary comparison job for the route and link results in the Linear ticket.
# Hold 1% for minimum duration specified in SLO gates doc (do not shorten).

h2. 4) Canary evaluation gates
During the canary window, continuously watch the required dashboards for the route.
The rollout may proceed only if all gates are green for the full window:
* error rate within allowed delta
* p95 latency within allowed delta
* saturation signals stable (GPU memory, queue depth)
* tail failures: timeouts, upstream 5xx, streaming disconnects
* quality signals (if enabled): eval harness regression checks, toxicity/safety guardrails

If any gate fails, follow the rollback runbook immediately.

h2. 5) Ramp schedule
Use the default ramp schedule unless explicitly approved otherwise:
# 1% for the minimum canary window
# 5% for 30 minutes
# 25% for 60 minutes
# 50% for 60 minutes
# 100% when gates remain green for 60 minutes at >= 50%

Notes:
* Use longer holds during peak traffic hours or after any warning-level anomaly.
* If the route has enterprise customers with strict SLOs, coordinate timing with Customer Success.

h2. 6) Finalize rollout
# Update the model registry: mark new version as "stable" and update "last_known_good" pointer for the route.
# Confirm alert routing and dashboards now track the stable version.
# Post completion message in #eng-releases with: start/end times, any anomalies, final version.
# If any customer comms were sent, post closure update per comms playbook.

h1. Post-rollout follow-ups
* Within 24 hours, check for slow-burn regressions (latency creep, elevated retries, memory fragmentation).
* If the rollout required rollback or significant tuning, file a short retrospective note in eng-platform/retrospectives.

h1. Common failure modes
* Streaming disconnects increase at >25%: suspect gateway timeout settings or upstream backpressure.
* Elevated 429/queue depth: capacity mis-match or batch config regression; coordinate with eng-sre and eng-infra.
* Quality regression without perf regression: confirm prompt-set coverage; consider partial rollout with customer allowlist.
